result.topic_en: Gauss sets up the geometry of three points with coordinates (a,b), (a',b'), (a'',b''), expresses the centre (ξ,η) and radius ρ of the circle through them, and introduces polar coordinates R, ψ about that centre to derive formulas for R²+ρ² and 2Rρ cos ψ from three ratios with weights m, m', m''.
result.transcription:
93.

$a''-a' = h\cos A$ \quad $a-a'' = h'\cos A'$ \quad $a'-a = h''\cos A''$
$b''-b' = h\sin A$ \quad $b-b'' = h'\sin A'$ \quad $b'-b = h''\sin A''$

Man hat dann

$\xi = a + h\sin(A'+A''-A) = a'+h'\sin(A''+A-A') = a''+h''\sin(A+A'-A'')$
$\eta = b - h\cos(A'+A''-A) = b' - h'\sin(A''+A-A') = b''-h''\cos(A+A'-A'')$
$\varrho = \frac{h}{\sin(A''-A')} = \frac{h'}{\sin(A-A'')} = \frac{h''}{\sin(A'-A)}$

Man nehme nun ferner an
$x = \xi + R\cos\psi$ \quad $y = \eta + R\sin\psi$
so findet man
$\frac{RR+\varrho\varrho - 2R\varrho\sin(\psi+A-A'-A'')}{mm} = \frac{RR+\varrho\varrho-2R\varrho\sin(\psi+A'-A''-A)}{m'm'}$
$= \frac{RR+\varrho\varrho-2R\varrho\sin(\psi+A''-A-A')}{m''m''} = \Delta$

Hieraus wird
I. $RR+\varrho\varrho = \frac{mm\sin(2A''-2A') + m'm'\sin(2A-2A'') + m''m''\sin(2A'-2A)}{4\sin(A''-A')\sin(A''-A)\sin(A'-A)}\Delta$

II. $2R\varrho\cos\psi = mmh\sin A + m'm'h'\sin A' + m''m''h''\sin A''$

$A$[?]
